messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Recap & next steps: CatalystMed discovery + topology questions

Hi Olivia / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we heard, confirmation of priorities, and proposed next steps. TL;DR: you want predictable latency for interactive routing, support for both chat and retrieval-augmented generation, and a deployment path that meets SOC2 + US data residency.

Pain points we captured:
- p50/p95 latency spikes for chat endpoints during morning batch jobs cause poor UX; need predictable P95 under load
- High memory usage from large-context conversations and embeddings; current infra can't sustain production peaks
- Procurement & compliance need a clear path for evidence (audit logs, retention) + an on-prem/VPC option for PHI workloads

Goals you stated:
- Interactive chat SLO: target P50 < 200ms, P95 < 500ms for 2k concurrent users (peak ~150 QPS across services)
- Embeddings throughput: ability to handle burst batch of 20k texts overnight without impacting daytime chat SLOs
- Data residency: primary in us-east with optional on-prem for PHI workloads

Technical notes / model requirements we discussed:
- Preferred model family: open-weight Llama2-70B-ish or equivalently performant model, quantized (8-bit/4-bit) for cost-efficiency
- KV cache and prefix caching will be important for long contexts (we recommended enabling KV cache across your chat route)
- Expectation for streaming responses and function-calling to the RAG layer

Deployment topology options (high level):
1) Hosted + Dedicated hybrid (recommended): hosted control plane + dedicated GPU pool for your tenant (predictable throughput, fast time-to-prod)
2) Private VPC (customer-managed networking): suitable for PHI, connects to your VPC via PrivateLink and supports KMS integration for key control
3) On-prem package (air-gapped): longer setup, required for regulated environments where no cloud egress is permitted

Attachments included: topology diagram (redwood-topology-options-v2.png), post-call notes (catalystmed-postcall-notes.pdf), mutual action plan (mutual-action-plan-202609.pdf).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Marissa to run a short topology fit: mapping model size + quantization profiles to expected QPS and SLOs (deliverable: capacity sketch) — due 2026-09-17
- Technical deep-dive with your infra + security (60m) to confirm network/KMS/retention: propose Thu 2026-09-16 10:00am ET — please confirm
- Procurement loop: I’ll share the high-level pricing bands and a canary proposal for a 30-day evaluation period targeted at non-PHI traffic

Can you confirm: 1) Thu 9/16 10am ET works for the deep-dive? 2) Peak QPS number — we noted ~150 but want confirmation.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Nikhil — great summary, appreciate the clear next steps. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming peak: our current estimate for peak interactive QPS is 140–160 across chat+search; 150 is a reasonable planning figure. Overnight embedding batches vary but typically ~15–25k docs.
- SLO tolerance: we can accept P95 up to 500ms during minor degradation windows, but long sessions (>10k tokens) need KV cache preservation; losing KV cache causes 3–4x latency increases in some cases.
- Compliance: SOC2 Type II in progress (expected in Q1 2027) — until then we need clear evidence trails (request: audit log retention of 90 days, ability to pull token-level request logs for investigations). For PHI workloads we will aim for private VPC or on-prem; timeline for PHI migration is TBD (not before Jan 2027).

Questions: 
1) Can you provide a rough cost ballpark for a dedicated pool that meets the above SLOs (150 QPS target, Llama2-70B quantized) — monthly committed cost range is fine for now.
2) For the deep-dive, please include a brief runbook for canarying (what metrics we should watch, how to rollback).

Thu 9/16 10am ET works for our infra + security (I’ll send calendar invites). Please include Marissa.

—Olivia

Perfect — thanks for the confirmation and for the extra details, Olivia. Calendar invite received; we’ll aim to keep the deep-dive to 60 minutes. Below is a short pre-read / canary runbook and a ballpark cost range so you have something to share with procurement ahead of the call. Marissa added a technical sketch below (forwarded).

Ballpark committed cost (high-level):
- Dedicated GPU pool (70B quantized, mixed precision, optimized kernels): $45k–$85k / month depending on burst allowance and retention of warm KV cache (lower end assumes tighter autoscaling + 4-bit quantization profile).
- Private VPC with control plane: add ~20–30% premium for networking, KMS/HSM integration, and additional compliance packaging.

Canary runbook (30-day recommended):
- Scope: non-PHI chat traffic to a single region (us-east) with a 10% traffic split initially
- Metrics to watch: P50/P95 latency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, error-rate (5xx/429), cost-per-1k-tokens
- Alerts: auto-fallback to smaller model variant if P95 > 750ms for >3m sustained
- Rollback: 1) reduce traffic split to 0% 2) re-route to hosted fallback model 3) collect full trace/log bundle for RCA

Forwarded message: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: RE: topology fit sketch for CatalystMed

Nikhil / Olivia — attaching a quick topology sketch here in text for the call. I’ll bring the PNG into the meeting.

- Assumptions: 150 QPS peak (concurrent ~2k users), average request size 800 tokens, spikes up to 10k-token sessions for some clinician workflows.
- Model profile: Llama2-70B quantized to 4-bit with optimized attention kernels. Expect token throughput ~400–600 tokens/sec per GPU for streaming; effective concurrency planning needs 6–10 GPUs for interactive SLOs depending on batching policy.
- Batching: use dynamic batching with a 25ms max latency window for batching; critical user-facing routes use smaller batch windows (~10–15ms) and higher priority queues.
- KV cache: persistent per-user KV cache stored in Redis-backed shards local to inference nodes (keeps warm cache; fallback to rewarm w/ small cost).
- Autoscale policy: baseline dedicated pool sized for 90% of daytime load, burst to a shared burst pool during predictable spikes; fallback rules to hosted smaller model for extreme overloads.
- Observability: token-level traces, per-route latency percentile dashboards, and automated quality checks (sanity evals) on canary responses.

Action items (Marissa): deliver capacity sketch and GPU count estimate by 2026-09-17; prepare a short slide for cost vs perf tradeoffs for Thu call.

—Marissa
